objective: Does the measured TCP heave and face tilt at gripping provide a better support datum at placement than the nominal taught flange pose?
design: Use public encoder minus spring JTS/K at grip rising, the taught pickup and placement frames and public nominal 6D site Jacobian. Map observed vs taught pickup pose into placement; correct normal translation and planar tilt only (no yaw or horizontal position target). A common scale caps heave at 1.5mm and tilt at 0.4deg. Smooth C2 turn-on over original final descent and return to the original reference 100ms after release. No pressure command, learned table force, hidden state, changed release time, detector coupling or gate change.
verification: For each mode four paired normal/offset and four matched impacts, same observed inputs until intervention. Compare normal original TCP RMS/peak, pickup/placement torque step and table force peak. Offline only: actual box bottom corners relative to level table, motion over last 20ms and at release, signed deviations, observer discrepancy; do not feed ground-truth force, height or grasp offset to controller or fit to it. If any normal G4/cost, FA, event or delay gate fails reject before independent validation. No fitting on impacts. No contact geometries or simulator changes.
scope: Finite development, not official and not universal: unknown initial offsets/compression and suction compliance can make taught pickup a bad datum.
